items.headline: Introducing WeatherNext 3, our most advanced and accurate global weather AI model
items.excerpt: DeepMind released WeatherNext 3, its most accurate global AI weather model to date, extending ensemble forecasting further ahead and at higher resolution than previous versions. The model is being made available through Google Cloud and Earth Engine for scientific and operational forecasting use.

items.headline: New Google DeepMind atlas could transform our understanding of genetic diseases
items.excerpt: Google DeepMind released AlphaGenome Atlas, a free database of predicted molecular effects for nine billion single-letter DNA variants across the human genome. Researchers can now look up a variant's likely regulatory impact instead of re-running the model or hunting through raw datasets.

items.headline: What OpenAI's latest controversy tells us about the future of math
items.excerpt: OpenAI says roughly 10,000 concurrent agents cracked a long-open problem in the Navier-Stokes family, but the claim is shadowed by accusations that it failed to credit the human mathematicians whose AI-assisted work it built on. The episode raises the question of whether frontier math now requires compute only a few labs can afford.

items.headline: How AI plotted an interstellar journey to Alpha Centauri
items.excerpt: An open-source agentic system called Get Physics Done broke an interstellar trajectory problem into sub-tasks, chose which simulations to run, and found a novel route for the Fermi Explorer Mission to Alpha Centauri. The 80,000-year trajectory was discovered by AI rather than hand-derived by mission planners.

items.headline: Live from ICM 2026: What Is Math For in the Age of AI?
items.excerpt: Recorded live at the International Congress of Mathematicians, Janna Levin and Steven Strogatz press working mathematicians on what remains uniquely human about their craft now that machines generate proofs. The conversation treats AI less as a tool question than as an identity question for the discipline.

items.headline: Release of open AI model trained on 17 years of lunar data maps ice, craters and volcanoes
items.excerpt: NASA and IBM released an open-source lunar foundation model trained on nearly two decades of Lunar Reconnaissance Orbiter data. It lets researchers identify ice deposits, impact craters and volcanic features with only minimal labeled training data.

items.headline: New AI model for DNA learns from evolution to unlock secrets of the human genome
items.excerpt: UC Berkeley's GPN-Star, a genomic language model trained on evolutionary signal, outperforms larger rivals at pinpointing the genetic variants behind inherited traits and disease. It does so while requiring far less compute to train than competing genomic foundation models.

items.headline: AI extracts interpretable constitutive laws directly from solid-mechanics data
items.excerpt: A graph-based framework from the Eastern Institute of Technology reads raw material-test data and writes out explicit, physically interpretable equations for how alloy steels, lithium metal and filled rubbers deform. It beat mainstream empirical models on predictive accuracy without becoming a black box.

items.headline: A connectomics milestone: Mapping the complete male fruit fly brain
items.excerpt: Google Research and collaborators used machine-learning segmentation to map the male fruit fly's entire brain and nervous system: 166,000 neurons and 125 million synapses, the largest brain map by neuron count so far. Paired with the earlier female map, it opens up comparative studies of courtship and aggression circuits.

items.headline: Transfer learning for genomic prediction in underrepresented populations
items.excerpt: A Google Research study finds that borrowing European genomic data helps small underrepresented cohorts, but actively hurts accuracy once the target population's own sample size grows. Trait-specific genetic architecture determines when external data should be dropped.

items.headline: An AI tool aims to catch harder-to-detect heart attacks in EKGs
items.excerpt: The FDA granted a rare de novo clearance to Powerful Medical's 'Queen of Hearts' algorithm, which reads electrocardiograms to flag and triage heart attacks that standard criteria miss. It is one of the first AI tools authorized for occlusion-type infarcts invisible to conventional EKG rules.

items.headline: Lancaster University Leads Project on Quantum Neural Computing
items.excerpt: Lancaster University is leading IgnisQNC, a EUR 1.88M three-year European project fusing quantum computing with explainable AI. The goal is to turn quantum uncertainty into a computational resource for trustworthy machine learning rather than a source of noise.
